{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 is reviewed using the supplied EFPA 2025 model, with AI systems as the assessed units. Evidence supports describing performance on unfamiliar grid tasks under specified conditions; broader reasoning interpretations remain unresolved. Ratings use the original key: n/a = inapplicable, 0 = insufficient evidence to rate, 1 = inadequate, 2 = adequate, 3 = good, 4 = excellent. Section judgments are qualitative, not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1 — Instrument: ARC-AGI-2 public test problems, official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; the cited technical report identifies François Chollet and colleagues. ARC Prize runs verified evaluations. Sources were inspected on 7 October 2026.",
        "2.1 — Content keywords: rule induction, grid transformation, reasoning. 2.2 — Area: AI benchmark research and system comparison. 2.3 — Intended assessed population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems. 2.4 — Users: researchers and system evaluators, inferred from the stated comparison use.",
        "2.5 — One overall problem-averaged score is described; separate scores established as distinct skill measures are not provided. 2.6 — Response mode: digitally submitted output grids. 2.9 — Production responses: generated grids, judged by task success. 2.10 — Stimuli: coloured two-dimensional grids and worked input-output examples.",
        "2.8 — Verified testing specifies AI settings and a spending limit and uses one run. Public practice tasks are separate from evaluation tasks. Other testing routes may differ.",
        "2.11 — There are 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120 problems each. The reviewed public test comprises 120 problems; each may contain multiple new inputs. 2.15 — Public, semi-private and private sets differ in access and were matched for human difficulty. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. 2.16 — Released sets have fixed problem content; no response-adaptive selection is described. 2.17 — The AI supplies task responses, rather than human self-report.",
        "3.1 — Direct digital scoring. 3.2 — Two attempts are permitted per new input; an exact match earns credit. Input credits are averaged within each problem, then problem scores are averaged. 3.3 — Raw task-success proportion. 3.4 — Standard-score transformation: n/a. 3.5 — No differentiated score norms are described; matching sets for human difficulty is not score norming.",
        "5.1 — Supporting material includes a technical report, public problems, running software, marking tests, policies and a dated change record. 5.2 — Publication includes public digital materials. Public data carry an Apache 2.0 licence; hidden-data policies cover confidentiality, provider handling and selected code review.",
        "General description — ARC-AGI-2 presents examples of coloured-grid transformations and asks an AI to generate outputs for new inputs. Its stated purpose is to assess working out unfamiliar rules and support investigation of broader reasoning. Development used human solving sessions, developer review and removal of repeated solution rules. Public, semi-private and private evaluation sets contain 120 problems each, alongside 1,000 development problems. The inspected software awards exact-match credit per input and averages within problems before averaging across problems. Verified evaluations specify conditions and use a single run.",
        "6.1.1 = 2 — The intended construct, inferring a new rule from examples, and its grid-task implementation are explained. This does not establish the broader intelligence claim. 6.1.2 = 2 — Human solving research and developer observations inform the rationale, with limited evidence beyond the grid domain.",
        "6.1.3, 6.1.3.1 = 2 — Design includes worked examples, novel inputs, exact-match scoring and separate development/evaluation sets; these fit the immediate task aim, although full design justifications are absent. 6.1.3.2 = 2 — Newly written and unused earlier puzzles, developer review and human solving provide a documented content-development process. 6.1.3.3 = 2 — Human difficulty matching and removal of repeated rules support final selection, but final-pool quantitative details are limited. 6.1.8 = 2 — Rationale and development are adequate for a grid-task benchmark, with item-quality evidence incomplete.",
        "6.2.1 = 3 — The immediate measurement aim and task logic are clear. 6.2.2 = 2 — Sources, human study and selection steps are described, but not fully linked to final-item results. 6.2.4 = 2 — Verified conditions and single-run policy provide some standardisation documentation. 6.2.13 = 2 — The supplied task and scoring descriptions are understandable; comprehensive inclusivity evidence is unavailable. 6.2.14 = 2 — Documentation adequately describes immediate use, with major technical gaps.",
        "6.3.1 = 2 — Task format, development/evaluation separation and verified-testing conditions are described. 6.3.2 = 2 — Exact-match and within-problem averaging rules are specified, and marking tests cover several error cases. 6.3.4 = 2 — Score meaning and the distinction between partial problem credit and fully solving a problem are explained. 6.3.7 = 2 — Evaluation-specific optimisation is discouraged and verified testing is not offered as repeated improvement feedback. 6.3.9 = 2 — The packet identifies the technical report and public technical materials. 6.3.10 = 2 — Basic procedures are adequately described, without comprehensive troubleshooting or interpretation guidance. 6.4 = 2 — Rationale and documentation support limited grid-performance use.",
        "7.1.2 = 2 — Worked transformations and an explicit output goal make the task understandable in the supplied description. 7.1.3 = 2 — Worked examples and public development tasks support familiarisation. 7.1.4 = 2 — The required output and two-attempt allowance are specified. 7.1.7 = 2 — Grid content is illustrated and has undergone review and correction. 7.1.8 = 2 — Materials appear adequate for the stated grid task, while operational robustness remains unverified.",
        "8.3.2.2 — The EFPA exception for raw-score comparisons is used: the reviewed comparison purpose does not require population norms or a competence cut-off. Human difficulty matching is not treated as a norm table or an AI performance standard.",
        "10.1 — Content evidence is addressed through 6.1: the examples, rule-induction task design, human solving and repeated-rule review support relevance to unfamiliar grid problems. They do not establish coverage of general intelligence.",
        "10.4.1 — Other evidence: design checks against repeated rules and extensive program search, exposure safeguards and correction history address some unintended routes or consequences. 10.4.2 = 2 — These are relevant development and governance procedures, although not comprehensive validation studies. 10.4.3 = 2 — They support cautious grid-task interpretation but do not establish immunity to alternative strategies.",
        "11.1.1 = 2 — The aim of requiring little specialist knowledge supports some consideration of broadly usable task content. 11.1.2 = 2 — Exposure rules and verified-condition policies provide some guidance for comparable use. 11.2 = 2 — Content review and repeated-rule checks support intended task access, without establishing equivalence across AI interfaces.",
        "Final evaluation — Strengths are a clear task, transparent scoring, separate development/evaluation sets, public technical materials and traceable corrections. The evidence supports inspecting observed grid-task success under declared conditions. Broader reasoning conclusions, equivalence across forms and precise rankings need additional evidence."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2; 6.3.2; 6.3.4 — The software permits partial credit within a problem, while dataset instructions reserve 'fully solved' for all inputs being correct. Reports must distinguish these quantities.",
        "6.1.3.3; 6.1.7 — Human study results cover a larger pool than the final test; they cannot automatically be attributed to every released item.",
        "7.1.7; 8.3.2.1 — The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples. Corrections do not automatically invalidate current items, but scores from different revisions need identification because affected AI scores are not all recalculated.",
        "9.3; 9.7 — Verified evaluations use one run. This limits inference about score precision; it is not evidence that repeated scores are unstable.",
        "10.4; 11.1.2 — Public evaluation problems are exposed, and hidden-data safeguards acknowledge possible leakage. Comparable exposure conditions cannot be assumed.",
        "9.4; 10.5 — Similar human difficulty across sets does not establish alternate-form equivalence or equal difficulty for AI systems.",
        "Final evaluation — No supplied study links these scores to language, social interaction or real-world work. Those interpretations remain unsupported by this packet, rather than disproved."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1 — Reviewer: anonymous AI simulation; review date and previous review date: not supplied. Local adaptation name, adaptation authors, local distributor and separate original publisher: not established. Current-edition, original-publication and adaptation-publication dates: not supplied. Source-inspection date is not a publication date.",
        "2.7 — Human attention, language command, language fluency, digital experience, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities, reading, vision and writing: n/a as human prerequisites. Reinterpreted prerequisites—supported grid encoding, colour representation, input/output capacity and instruction handling—are not fully specified.",
        "2.11 — Minimum, maximum and typical new-input counts per problem are absent. 2.12.1 — Individual AI evaluation is implied; batch/group administration is not specified. 2.12.2 — Verified evaluation controls conditions, but the precise mapping to EFPA supervision categories is unspecified. 2.13 — Digital execution is required; hardware, connectivity and supported interfaces are not detailed.",
        "2.14 — Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and stakeholder-feedback times are not supplied. Automated functions may require zero administrator time under EFPA guidance, but the extent of automation is not sufficiently documented to assign those times.",
        "4.1 — Digital outputs and problem scores are said to be released; an interpretive report product and report count are not established. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 — Report names, design and structure are unspecified. 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 — Context sensitivity, report-development method and modifiability are unspecified. 4.8 — Score calculation is transparent, but a score-to-report-text mapping is not supplied. 4.9, 4.10 — Report content and intended recipient categories are not established.",
        "5.3 — Supplier-required user qualifications are not stated; this is not evidence that no qualifications are required.",
        "6.1.5 — Psychometric framework: not specified. Human solving informs difficulty, but final-item difficulty indices, means/SDs, item-total correlations, IRT parameters, distractor analyses and DIF results are not supplied. 6.1.6 = 0 — Quantitative item-analysis methodology is insufficiently detailed. 6.1.7 = 0 — Final-pool quantitative item-quality results are insufficient.",
        "6.2.6 = 0 — Reliability methods and results are absent. 6.2.7 = 2 — Some content-development evidence is described, but expert numbers, qualifications and agreement statistics are incomplete. 6.2.8 = 0 — Internal-structure evidence is absent. 6.2.9 = 0 — Relationships with external variables are insufficiently documented. 6.2.10 = 2 — Alternative-route and exposure procedures are described, without comprehensive outcome evidence. 6.2.11 = 0 — Guidance covering relevant AI subgroup fairness is insufficient. 6.2.12 = 0 — Interpretive-report documentation is unavailable.",
        "6.3.6 = 0 — Guidance on differential AI performance and bias is insufficient. 6.3.8 = 0 — Full software requirements, failure handling and technical support are not supplied.",
        "7.1.1 = 0 — End-to-end operational robustness was not independently checked. 7.1.5 = 0 — Interface design evidence is insufficient. 7.1.6 = 0 under the AI-access reinterpretation — Equivalent access across encodings, interfaces or model modalities is untested.",
        "8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.1.3, 8.1.3.1, 8.1.3.2, 8.1.3.3, 8.1.4 — n/a: no norm-referenced score interpretation is established; local relevance, norm representativeness, classical/continuous sample size, modelling and norm sampling therefore do not apply. The 407 human participants and 515 sessions are not treated as an AI norm sample.",
        "8.2.1, 8.2.1.1, 8.2.1.2, 8.2.1.3, 8.2.1.4, 8.2.1.5, 8.2.2 — n/a: no competence cut score is described, so judge selection, numbers, standard setting, agreement methods/results and empirical threshold validation are inapplicable. Exact-match item scoring is not a competence threshold.",
        "8.3.1, 8.3.2, 8.3.2.1, 8.3.2.3, 8.3.3 — n/a for norm adequacy, age and norm-based fairness. Revision comparability remains relevant independently of norms.",
        "9.1 — No score reliability coefficient or measurement-error estimate is supplied. 9.2, 9.2.1, 9.2.2, 9.2.3, 9.2.4 — n/a for the reviewed heterogeneous task-success composite; no reflective, homogeneous scale is established. This does not remove the requirement for other precision evidence.",
        "9.3, 9.3.1 = 0, 9.3.2 = 0 — Same-system repeatability sample sizes and coefficients are absent. 9.3.3 — Repeat interval: not supplied. 9.3.4 — Matching of a retest sample to intended AI systems: not supplied.",
        "9.4, 9.4.1 = 0, 9.4.2 = 0 — AI alternate-form sample sizes and equivalence coefficients are absent. 9.4.3 — Sample matching is unknown. Human difficulty matching is not substituted for these data.",
        "9.5, 9.5.1, 9.5.2, 9.5.3 — n/a: no IRT scoring or latent-trait precision method is described. 9.6, 9.6.1, 9.6.2, 9.6.3 — n/a for deterministic exact-match response scoring, which involves no scorer judgment.",
        "9.7, 9.7.1 = 0, 9.7.3 = 0 — No alternative score-precision study is supplied. 9.7.2 — Method: none established; systematic prompt, presentation and software sensitivity studies are absent. 9.8 = 0 — Overall precision cannot be rated from the supplied evidence; this is a critical evidence gap.",
        "10.2, 10.2.1 — No internal-structure or AI DIF technique is supplied. 10.2.2 = 0, 10.2.3 = 0 — Dimensionality and invariance are unestablished; absence of subscale scores does not establish a single latent reasoning dimension.",
        "10.3.1, 10.3.1.1 — A human background-factor association study is described; techniques and detailed results are not supplied. 10.3.1.2 = 0 — No justified AI-group difference hypotheses and results are supplied. 10.3.1.3 = 0, 10.3.1.4 = 0 — Convergent and discriminant correlations are absent. 10.3.1.5 = n/a — No MTMM design is described. 10.3.1.6 = 0 — No systematic experimental evidence for administration changes is supplied. 10.3.1.7 = 0 — The human background finding is insufficient to validate AI score interpretations.",
        "10.3.1.8 = 0 — Relevant AI validation sample sizes are absent; the human development-study count does not fill this role. 10.3.1.9 = 0 — Marker quality is unestablished. 10.3.1.10 — Validation-study collection dates are absent. 10.3.1.11 = 0 — External-relationship evidence is insufficient.",
        "10.3.2, 10.3.2.1 — No predictive, concurrent or postdictive external-criterion study is supplied. 10.3.2.2 = 0, 10.3.2.3 = 0, 10.3.2.4 = 0 — Relevant sample size, criterion quality and relationship strength are unavailable. 10.3.2.5 = n/a — No diagnostic classification use is stated. 10.3.2.6 — Study age: unknown. 10.3.2.7 = 0 — Criterion validity remains unresolved.",
        "10.5 = 0 for broader reasoning/general-intelligence interpretation — Content relevance to grids is documented, but evidence sufficient to rate the broader inference is absent. This critical rating does not mean observed grid answers were scored incorrectly.",
        "11.3 = 0 — AI subgroup piloting and DIF evidence are absent. 11.4 = 0 — Comparable subgroup precision is unestablished. 11.5 = 0 — Comparable subgroup validity is unestablished. 11.7 = 0 — Report fairness cannot be assessed without report specimens. 11.8 = 0 — Overall support for fair AI comparisons is insufficiently evidenced; this is not a finding of demonstrated bias.",
        "12.1 = 0, 12.2 = 0, 12.3 = 0, 12.4 = 0, 12.5 = 0, 12.6 = 0, 12.7 = 0 — Under a provisional digital-score-report interpretation, scope, consistency, validity, fairness, acceptability, detail and overall adequacy cannot be evaluated: three actual score-profile reports required by EFPA are not supplied. The worked scoring illustration is not an observed AI report.",
        "Final evaluation: critical attributes — 9.8 precision and 10.5 validity for broader inference receive 0. Under EFPA guidance, use dependent on these interpretations should be restricted to research or exceptional expert use; this is an evidence limitation, not demonstrated technical inadequacy. Conclusions — Users need competence in AI evaluation, scoring, exposure control and uncertainty; correspondence with supplier qualification requirements cannot be checked.",
        "Summary of Ratings — 6.4: 2; 7.1.8: 2; 7.2.7: n/a; 8.3.3: n/a; 9.8: 0; 10.5: 0 for broader inference; 11.8: 0; 12.7: 0 provisionally. No cross-section aggregate is calculated.",
        "Part C — Sources used: only the supplied ARC-AGI-2 passage and supplied EFPA 2025 extraction. Benchmark report, software and policies are known through that passage, not independently consulted. No additional bibliography details are invented."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "EFPA attribution — European Federation of Psychologists’ Associations AISBL (2025), Model for the Review, Description and Evaluation of Psychological and Educational Tests, version 5.0; supplied source https://www.efpa.eu/; CC BY-SA 4.0. This is an application with explicit AI reinterpretations, not EFPA endorsement.",
        "2.3, 2.7, 2.8, 2.12.1, 2.12.2, 2.13, 2.17 — Test taker means the configured AI system; administrator means its evaluator. Human identity controls become system/configuration provenance. Human disability and bodily prerequisites are inapplicable; technical representational access is evaluated separately.",
        "6.1.4, 6.2.3 — n/a: no translated or local adapted benchmark is described. Changes in prompts or grid encoding are administration variants requiring evidence, not documented language adaptations.",
        "6.2.5, 6.3.3 — n/a: no norm transformations are used. 6.3.5 — Human test-taker debriefing is n/a; stakeholder explanation remains relevant, but guidance for it is not supplied, rated 0 under that reinterpretation.",
        "7.1.6; 11.1–11.5 — Human accessibility categories are not directly assigned to AI systems. Relevant comparisons concern interfaces, representations, system configurations and exposure conditions; human participant background findings do not establish fairness across these AI conditions.",
        "7.2, 7.2.1, 7.2.2, 7.2.3, 7.2.4, 7.2.5, 7.2.6, 7.2.7 — n/a: the reviewed benchmark uses digital task materials. The summary table's reference to 7.2.8 conflicts with the supplied section ending at 7.2.7; 7.2.8 is recorded as an apparent cross-reference error, not an additional rated item.",
        "8; 11.6, 11.6.1, 11.6.2 — Norm and threshold fairness are n/a for raw task-performance comparison. Human difficulty matching and exact-match answer keys are not reclassified as population norms or competence standards.",
        "9 — An individual assessed unit is an AI system under declared conditions. Human sample-size thresholds are not applied to puzzle counts or session counts as if those were independent AI systems.",
        "4; 12 — Digital score outputs are provisionally treated as reports to retain coverage. Narrative report availability is unestablished; all report ratings are 0 for missing specimens, rather than claims of poor report quality.",
        "Coverage — Every supplied numbered descriptive field and rated item is explicitly addressed, including conditional subareas. Non-rated parent headings are covered by their child entries. No item omission is intentional."
      ],
      "closing_note": "The supplied description leaves 'fully solved' versus software partial credit easy to confuse, and does not fully specify administration or revision comparability. The EFPA extraction also contains report-anchor wording and numbering inconsistencies; these were recorded without substituting another instrument."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA is reviewed using the supplied EFPA 2025 model, with AI systems and their information-supply pipelines as assessed units. The evidence supports examining performance on the specified Formula SAE tasks; broader engineering competence and fine ranking differences remain unresolved. Ratings use the original key: n/a = inapplicable, 0 = insufficient evidence to rate, 1 = inadequate, 2 = adequate, 3 = good, 4 = excellent. Section judgments are qualitative, not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1 — Instrument: original DesignQA benchmark described in the 2024 paper and its public scoring software. Developers: researchers and engineers using Formula SAE materials. Sources were inspected on 6 October 2026; later revisions may affect results.",
        "2.1 — Content keywords: engineering-rule retrieval, document understanding, design assessment. 2.2 — Area: AI engineering-document evaluation. 2.3 — Intended assessed population: AI systems answering questions about rules, drawings and vehicle designs. 2.4 — Users: researchers and AI evaluators, inferred from the stated comparison purpose.",
        "2.5 — Six question groups and an equal-weight overall score are described. The groups concern individual-rule retrieval, related-rule retrieval, technical terminology, component presence, dimensional compliance and functional performance; none is established as a distinct latent skill scale.",
        "2.6 — Digital text and yes/no responses, sometimes with explanations. 2.8 — Instructions, model settings and information supply vary by evaluated system; some receive the rulebook and others retrieved passages. 2.9 — Open text and binary selection responses. 2.10 — Written rules, vehicle images and drawings.",
        "2.11 — The paper reports 1,451 question-answer pairs: 1,192 individual-rule questions and 16 functional-performance questions are specified in the packet. 2.15 — Six task groups and experimental input variants are described, rather than demonstrated equivalent forms. 2.16 — A fixed question collection is described; retrieval changes the information supplied, not a documented adaptive test design. 2.17 — The AI supplies answers; engineering contributors and reviewers supply reference content.",
        "3.1 — Digital scoring of submitted answers. 3.2 — Text comparison and yes/no correctness are used; explanations may receive similarity scores. The overall software score weights each group equally. 3.3 — Raw accuracy/similarity-based group measures and a composite. 3.4 — Standard-score transformations: n/a. 3.5 — No differentiated population norms are described.",
        "5.1 — Materials include a paper, public questions, instructions, scoring code, some AI responses and small marking-test files. 5.2 — Public digital materials are available.",
        "General description — DesignQA contains 1,451 reported question-answer pairs based on one Formula SAE rulebook, vehicle designs and test data. Six groups address rule retrieval, terminology, component recognition, dimensions and functional requirements. AI systems receive text, images or drawings and return text or yes/no answers, sometimes with explanations. Scores use several marking methods, and the software combines the six group results with equal weights. The paper reports AI comparisons, baselines and input-manipulation studies. Results describe performance on these tasks with each system's supplied information.",
        "6.1.1 = 2 — The rationale links finding, understanding and applying engineering information to selected engineering activities. 6.1.2 = 2 — Reported AI comparisons and input manipulations provide empirical context, without establishing broad engineering competence.",
        "6.1.3, 6.1.3.1 = 2 — The six task types have a clear practical rationale, although composite weighting and group balance are insufficiently justified. 6.1.3.2 = 2 — Real rules, designs, test data and practitioner/researcher contributions support task relevance. 6.1.3.3 = 0 — Evidence explaining final-item selection and coverage is insufficient. 6.1.8 = 2 — Development has a credible task-content basis, with important selection and item-quality gaps.",
        "6.2.1 = 3 — The intended tasks and engineering motivation are clearly described. 6.2.2 = 2 — Item sources and review procedures are described, with explicit exceptions. 6.2.4 = 1 — Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to each reported result, limiting reproducible standardisation. 6.2.7 = 2 — Content checking is described, but qualifications, agreement and residual error are incompletely documented.",
        "6.2.9 = 2 — AI and random baselines and input-manipulation studies are reported, with limitations on their interpretation. 6.2.10 = 2 — Wording, retrieval, familiarity and exposure concerns receive discussion. 6.2.13 = 2 — The supplied task descriptions and acknowledged limitations are understandable; broad inclusivity evidence is unavailable. 6.2.14 = 2 — Documentation supports inspection of the tasks, with incomplete reproducibility and measurement support.",
        "6.3.1 = 2 — Instructions and settings are described for reported systems. 6.3.2 = 2 — Scoring methods are explained and have some marking tests, though comprehensive correctness checks are absent. 6.3.4 = 2 — The paper acknowledges limited generalisation and imperfect scoring. 6.3.9 = 2 — The paper and public materials provide supporting references at the level described in the packet. 6.3.10 = 2 — Basic procedures are usable for exploratory evaluation, with substantial omissions. 6.4 = 2 — Rationale and documentation are adequate for limited task analysis.",
        "7.1.2 = 2 — Question categories and expected response types are understandable. 7.1.3 = 2 — Public questions and instructions support task familiarisation. 7.1.4 = 2 — Text and binary response requirements are described.",
        "8.3.2.2 — The EFPA exception for raw-score comparison is used: the stated benchmark comparison purpose does not require population norms or an engineering-competence cut-off. Correct yes/no labels are item keys, not competence standards.",
        "10.1 — Content evidence is addressed through 6.1: authentic rulebook, vehicle and test materials and engineering review support relevance to the selected tasks. They do not establish representative engineering-domain coverage.",
        "10.3.1.1 — Techniques include AI/random-baseline comparisons and experimental input changes. 10.3.1.6 = 2 — Manipulating passages, dimensions, scale bars and highlighting provides some evidence about input dependence, though detailed study adequacy is limited.",
        "10.4.1 — Other evidence concerns formatting effects, reference-answer incompleteness, component familiarity and unintended strategies. 10.4.2 = 2 — Examples and focused checks provide some credible evidence about alternative score influences. 10.4.3 = 1 — Documented formatting penalties and a constant-answer route undermine interpreting all awarded credit as engineering understanding.",
        "Final evaluation — Strengths include authentic engineering materials, task-specific questions, some additional content review, public scoring resources and explicit discussion of limitations. Results can support exploratory analysis of these questions under disclosed information-supply conditions."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "2.11; 3.2; 6.1.3.1 — Group sizes are highly uneven, while the overall software score weights groups equally. This makes the composite sensitive to its weighting choice; a distinct common skill interpretation is not established.",
        "3.2; 6.3.2 — Scoring examples show penalties from missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers. Awarded credit can therefore reflect formatting and answer-key coverage.",
        "6.1.3.2; 10.1 — One rulebook and limited task types constrain content coverage. Authenticity does not establish representativeness across engineering industries.",
        "6.2.4; 7.1.1 — Exact historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every result. One released answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count.",
        "7.1.7 = 1 — Some documented reference-answer and formatting problems can penalise valid responses. This item-content judgment concerns the identified scoring materials, not an asserted error rate across all questions. 7.1.8 = 1 — Documented content/key problems limit adequacy of the scored digital materials.",
        "9.7; 10.3.1.6 — Testing one AI with five passage sets measures variation under changed information; it does not isolate identical-condition repeatability.",
        "10.4.3 — All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, so constant 'yes' responses would obtain binary credit on that portion. This does not demonstrate that a tested AI used that strategy.",
        "11.1.2 = 1 — Systems receive materially different information supplies. Comparisons require interpreting the model and its retrieval/context pipeline together.",
        "5.1; 6.2.4 — Revision history exists, but a clear explanation of revision effects on scores was not found. Historical results cannot automatically be transferred to the current release.",
        "9.8; Final evaluation — The 16-question performance group has coarse score resolution: the passage states one answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points. Reported information does not support confident interpretation of small main-comparison differences."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1 — Reviewer: anonymous AI simulation; review date and previous review date: not supplied. Individual authors, local adaptation name/authors, local distributor and separate original publisher: not identified. Original publication year: 2024; exact publication date, current-revision publication date and local-adaptation date: not supplied.",
        "2.7 — Human attention, language command, language fluency, digital experience, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities, reading, vision and writing: n/a as human prerequisites. Reinterpreted requirements—text/image handling, context capacity and access to necessary rule information—are only partially specified.",
        "2.11 — Counts for the other four groups and reconciliation of the shorter released answer file are absent. 2.12.1 — Individual AI evaluation is implied; group/batch administration is unspecified. 2.12.2 — Degree of supervision and control of system provenance is not fully described. 2.13 — Digital execution is required; complete hardware, connectivity and interface requirements are absent.",
        "2.14 — Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and stakeholder-feedback times are not supplied. EFPA assigns zero administrator time to automated functions, but the packet does not establish which full procedures are automated.",
        "4.1 — Software score outputs and some AI responses exist; an interpretive report product and report count are not established. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 — Report names, presentation and structure are unspecified beyond group/composite scores. 4.5, 4.6, 4.7 — Context sensitivity, report-development method and modifiability are unspecified. 4.8 — Some scoring linkage is described, but report-text linkage is not supplied. 4.9, 4.10 — Interpretive content and intended recipient categories are not established.",
        "5.3 — Supplier-required user qualifications are unspecified. A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials; this does not establish that permission is unavailable or reuse prohibited.",
        "6.1.5 — Psychometric framework: not specified. No final-item difficulty/discrimination table, item-total correlations, IRT parameters, distractor analysis or DIF results are supplied. 6.1.6 = 0 — Systematic item-analysis methodology is insufficiently described. 6.1.7 = 0 — Quantitative item-quality results are insufficient.",
        "6.2.6 = 0 — Same-condition precision methods and results are unavailable. 6.2.8 = 0 — Internal structure is unestablished. 6.2.11 = 0 — Guidance covering relevant AI-group fairness and comparable information access is insufficient. 6.2.12 = 0 — Interpretive-report documentation is unavailable.",
        "6.3.6 = 0 — Practical bias guidance across AI comparison conditions is insufficient. 6.3.7 = 0 — Clear rules for training on released questions, repeated submissions and restrictions on use are unavailable. 6.3.8 = 0 — Full requirements, troubleshooting and technical support are unspecified.",
        "7.1.1 = 0 — End-to-end software robustness is unestablished; small marking tests do not establish complete reliability. 7.1.5 = 0 — User-interface design is insufficiently described. 7.1.6 = 0 under the AI-access reinterpretation — Equivalent accessibility across text/image capabilities and information-supply arrangements is unestablished.",
        "8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.1.3, 8.1.3.1, 8.1.3.2, 8.1.3.3, 8.1.4 — n/a: no norm-referenced interpretation is established, so local relevance, representativeness, classical/continuous sample sizes, continuous modelling and norm sampling do not apply. AI/random baselines are not population norms.",
        "8.2.1, 8.2.1.1, 8.2.1.2, 8.2.1.3, 8.2.1.4, 8.2.1.5, 8.2.2 — n/a: no competence cut score is supplied; judge selection, numbers, standard setting, agreement methods/results and empirical threshold validation do not apply.
